avenues.objective: Test whether Fabric versus NeoForge plus an unsupported-version control are materially different when agents must boot, save, reload and upgrade a minimal logical-server player mod across pinned Java Edition builds; measure clean startup, lifecycle hook coverage and upgrade compatibility per version.
approaches: Comparison candidates and controls: Fabric versus NeoForge plus an unsupported-version control.
Run matched trials and independent holdout worlds or deterministic fault schedules, as appropriate; preserve unsuccessful attempts.
Audit server-authoritative legal actions and information-access boundaries, without crediting scripts as learned ability.
avenues.benefit: Could improve loader and game-version compatibility policy while preserving Minecraft grounding and per-agent continuity.
avenues.limitations: Fabric 26.3/Java 25 booted and executed a dedicated-server GameTest in CI #76, but only a fixture world assertion was run. No ServerPlayer-compatible AI, client, integrated world, save/migration, NeoForge comparator, or unsupported-version control was tested.
avenues.computationalRequirements: Unknown until the protocol and candidate scale are fixed. Record CPU/GPU model, memory, wall time, inference rate and energy/cost when measured; start with a bounded baseline.
avenues.implementationRequirements: A version-pinned native interface or isolated research harness for loader and game-version compatibility policy, structured logging, deterministic fixtures where possible, timeout/recovery behavior and tests for the contract.
avenues.methodology: Pin Minecraft/mod/server versions and legal observation/action budgets. Reproduce: boot, save, reload and upgrade a minimal logical-server player mod across pinned Java Edition builds. Compare: Fabric versus NeoForge plus an unsupported-version control. Record: clean startup, lifecycle hook coverage and upgrade compatibility per version. Inject boundary: missing loader hooks, mismatched mappings or corrupted data migration.
acceptanceCriteria: Set up a reproducible fixture for boot, save, reload and upgrade a minimal logical-server player mod across pinned Java Edition builds; declare initial state, server/game build, observation budget and control conditions.

Report clean startup, lifecycle hook coverage and upgrade compatibility per version separately for Fabric versus NeoForge plus an unsupported-version control, including failed and inconclusive trials; never require a positive outcome to complete research.
Exercise missing loader hooks, mismatched mappings or corrupted data migration; verify exact side effects and document unsafe, incompatible or unresolvable cases.
Publish pinned revisions, task distributions, seeds or deterministic fault schedule, raw evidence, reproduction commands, statistical uncertainty where relevant and limitations.
avenues.conclusion: Pinned Fabric 26.3 mod and evaluator-only dedicated-server GameTest booted in CI #76. This confirms one narrow loader/server smoke case, not MI-004 compatibility or player embodiment acceptance.
openQuestions: Which of Fabric versus NeoForge plus an unsupported-version control withstands missing loader hooks, mismatched mappings or corrupted data migration with the best clean startup, lifecycle hook coverage and upgrade compatibility per version?

avenues.title: Shared-resource contention and cooperative deadlock recovery
avenues.objective: Test shared-resource contention and cooperative deadlock recovery in the following native Minecraft case: Assign four AI players overlapping chest access, furnace queues and scaffold positions on a joint build.
approaches: Experiment candidate; no architecture selected until matched controls, resource budgets and negative trials are evaluated.
Compare against independent uncoordinated policies and scripted centralized allocation with legal actions.
Use identical legal action and allowed observation budgets across trials.
avenues.benefit: May improve agent capability or efficiency measured by deadlock incidence, mean wait ticks, fairness, task throughput and contested-resource corruption, subject to trials and feasibility.
avenues.limitations: Uninvestigated in MNI. Minecraft/loader-specific execution, model availability and prior-work transfer are unverified; permanent waiting cycles, stale reservation after death and one agent accessing another private memory must be detected and recovered.
avenues.computationalRequirements: No measurements yet. Record CPU/GPU model, peak RAM/VRAM, game MSPT/TPS, per-agent inference rate and total wall-clock time; compare at a bounded fixed budget.
avenues.implementationRequirements: Native observation/action contracts, version-pinned Java Edition environment or explicitly labelled isolated harness, deterministic trace capture, cancellation and failure recording.
avenues.methodology: Fixture: Assign four AI players overlapping chest access, furnace queues and scaffold positions on a joint build. Comparator: independent uncoordinated policies and scripted centralized allocation with legal actions. Outcomes: deadlock incidence, mean wait ticks, fairness, task throughput and contested-resource corruption. Falsifier: permanent waiting cycles, stale reservation after death and one agent accessing another private memory must be detected and recovered.
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce the fixture: Assign four AI players overlapping chest access, furnace queues and scaffold positions on a joint build.

Publish matched comparator trials against independent uncoordinated policies and scripted centralized allocation with legal actions, including deadlock incidence, mean wait ticks, fairness, task throughput and contested-resource corruption.
Exercise the negative boundary: permanent waiting cycles, stale reservation after death and one agent accessing another private memory must be detected and recovered.

Record scenario/checkpoint versions, held-out seeds, legal action and observation parity, raw traces, failure taxonomy, hardware budget and uncertainty. A negative result can conclude the research, not implement the capability.
avenues.conclusion: Candidate only. No MNI experiment, integration, verification or in-game success evidence exists.

Communication demonstrably conditions on world state, memory, relationships and outcomes through aligned human/agent pathways
Agents generate and revise activities without constant instruction and measure/bound scripted contribution

Persistent concurrent agents avoid identity leakage and report emergence and failure in social/communication evaluations
Batched shared inference, low-frequency cognition, profiling and accelerated/replayable simulation support larger populations
Major subsystems run together in a persistent experimental world with end-to-end observability and reproducibility
Stable documented research platform publishes the strongest validated results and limitations

scoring.researchCoverage: Complete catalog coverage means every declared avenue, model candidate and training method has the required objective, scope, alternatives/prior work, dependencies, acceptance criteria, status, evidence links and remaining work. This is research-space coverage, not literature-review completion.
scoring.weighting: Each item contributes workstream weight (1-5) × item priority (1-5). Weights express project-objective relevance and relative priority. The core capability workstreams (Minecraft integration, perception, action, models, learning, cognition, construction, memory, language/social and multi-agent infrastructure) use higher weights than supporting operations; evaluation and safety remain high because capability claims require them.
scoring.demonstratedCapability: A capability contributes only when its outcome is positive, implementation is functional or later, validation is in-game or stronger, main revision provenance is current, and an independently reviewed evidence record satisfies its acceptance criteria. PR-only code, synthetic-only results and passing unit/compile checks do not qualify.
scoring.formula: All percentages are weighted means over the same canonical items. Research completion uses research state. Experimental effectiveness is positive-outcome rate, not research completion. Implementation maturity, validation and readiness use independent maps. Overall scoped progress = 0.60×demonstrated capability + 0.20×implementation maturity + 0.10×validation coverage + 0.10×production readiness; documentation and catalog coverage have no direct contribution. Milestones use equal-weight exit criteria (open=0, prototype=0.25, partial=0.5, met=1), mapped to avenues/candidates/methods and main-branch evidence.
scoring.limitations: No aggregate is an intelligence, autonomy, consciousness or human-level score. Negative research can reach 100% completion while effectiveness and capability remain zero. Scope expansion or correcting unsupported statuses can lower indicators. A zero is absence of qualifying evidence in this dataset, not proof unrecorded work never occurred.

experimentRecords.datasetVersion: terrain-encoding geometry fixture v1; scenario SHA-256 7b8e40801c75af4e1b033753d177170181c49d2089fb9b2571df3494e6b90a8c.
experimentRecords.configuration: 35 logical trials: 7 encoders × 5 fixed seeds; 120-second per-trial timeout; clean source revision; run manifest SHA-256 53756ae112c9cf892ae0b809f57138fb4309bd6d3ea86fd8f3786ae07cba788e. Variants: dense, sparse, octree, graph, egocentric-slices, chunk-features, change-events.
experimentRecords.hardware: Windows 10 AMD64, Intel64 Family 6 Model 183 Stepping 1 CPU; GPU not used or recorded.
experimentRecords.methodology: Compare lossless/local visible-sample terrain encodings on synthetic geometry cases for fidelity, payload size, and encode/decode median latency; hidden-world perturbation checks are included.
experimentRecords.reproduction: Closed unmerged PR #123 at exact reviewed head 59695fc66442b3628fccfd4051fa3117191f7959; use experiments/terrain-encoding/experiment.json and the referenced committed result bundle. The run itself records source revision 0c0558f651acd2d2905a3658b11677fcfda8902e.
experimentRecords.limitations: Synthetic geometry only; no Minecraft chunks, live player observations, agent policy, downstream navigation/building outcome, or generalization result. Thirty terrain cases and five seeds do not establish statistical superiority. Dense and several encodings reconstruct supplied visible samples exactly; chunk-features are lossy. Similar low position-overlap metrics across variants indicate this run does not establish representation quality for agent capability. Branch result has not merged and is not credited as an integrated feature.
experimentRecords.hardwareNotes: Benchmark timing is local CPU microbenchmark data; do not compare across machines without controls.
